subject: ventures/mechanics-lien-deadline-calculator
auditor: agent session (Claude), independent audit subagent, see run record
professional: a construction lawyer who files mechanics liens for subcontractors and suppliers in several states; first checks: the statutory trigger event and day count per state, first-tier versus lower-tier clocks, and whether the tool ever shows a date later than the true one

evidence.correctness: Ran `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in the venture dir: 34 pass, 0 fail. Recomputed 8 outputs by running calc.mjs and comparing to independent Python date arithmetic (datetime) and to the statutes as I know them (statute hosts were NOT fetched; leginfo curl was attempted but I did not rely on it, and no statute text was opened, so confidence is moderate and the score is capped at 2 accordingly): CA first 2026-03-10 -> prelim 2026-03-30 (Cal. Civ. Code 8200, 20 days) matches; CA completion 2026-06-25 -> lien 2026-09-23 (8412, 90 days) matches Python; CA with NOC 2026-07-01 -> 2026-07-31 (8412, 30 days for non-original-contractor claimants) matches; FL first 2026-01-15 -> 2026-03-01 (Fla. Stat. 713.06(2)(a), 45 days) and last 2026-03-01 -> 2026-05-30, safe date Fri 05-29 (713.08(5), 90 days) match; AZ completion 2026-05-10 -> 2026-09-07 (A.R.S. 33-993, 120 days) and NOC path -> Aug 30 shown as safe Aug 28 (60 days) match; WA residential first 2026-02-20 -> 2026-03-02 (RCW 60.04.031, 10 days), last 2026-12-31 -> 2027-03-31 (60.04.091, 90 days) match; GA first 2026-02-01 -> 2026-03-03, last 2026-12-31 -> 2027-03-31 (O.C.G.A. 44-14-361.1/361.5) match; TX commercial first 2026-10-05 -> 2027-01-15 (3rd month after October, Tex. Prop. Code 53.056), last 2026-11-20 -> 2027-03-15 (53.052, 4th month) match, with year rollover correct. All eight agree with my arithmetic and my recollection of the statutes. Not verified: the Texas residential subcontractor lien clock after the 2022 amendments (HB 2237), the Georgia 'later of' notice trigger, and the AZ/CA cessation-notice paths. Reading plus these runs; no authoritative statute text was opened, so not 3.
evidence.completeness: Checked each README/page feature by running it: both dates for six states (CA, TX, FL, AZ, WA, GA) work; weekend flag and last-business-day safe date work (mutation below proved it is tested); days remaining and passed/soon/today status work (calc tests 'status reflects days remaining'); TX commercial/residential and WA residential splits work; CA/AZ notice-of-completion shortening works; unsupported state throws; invalid or reversed dates compute nothing. page.test.mjs (run, passing) checks the page wiring; I did not load the page in a browser. README 'What this does not cover' honestly lists out-of-scope items. Stubs/TODOs: none found. Stale items: VENTURE.yaml description and index.html JSON-LD featureList still say five states, and the FAQ JSON-LD and on-page FAQ omit Georgia.
evidence.verification: `node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 34 tests pass in about 0.4 s. Seeded mutation 1 in resolveLien: reversed the sort in the earlier_of_completion branch (`b.date - a.date`, picks the LATER of completion/NOC dates, an unsafe-direction bug): caught by 2 tests (CA notice-of-completion test, AZ test); reverted with git checkout. Mutation 2: previousBusinessDay returns the input unchanged: caught (weekend test and the page worked-example test). Mutation 3: isWeekend ignores Saturday: caught (weekend test and page test). All reverted; `git status --short` on the venture dir is clean. Weaknesses: tests are hand-picked examples by the author, with no property test for 'safe date never later than statutory date' and no cross-check against any external source of truth; Texas residential lien date has one test.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (360 lines), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, usage.mjs, index.html script. Clean: pure functions, rule table (STATE_RULES) separated from resolvers, UTC-only date math with round-trip validation in parseDate, no dependencies, unsupported state throws rather than guessing, ISO-only parsing. Defects: (1) `today` in the page is built from the local clock while all deadlines are UTC midnight, fine for day counts but undocumented; (2) the 'safe date' always rolls back on weekends even where the state rolls forward, shown as such, acceptable; (3) the `status` object is computed against safeDate, so 'passed' can read slightly differently from the statutory date, minor; (4) two-tier rule objects (prelimByProject / prelim) make the lookup branch awkward but readable; (5) no handling of holidays (documented). No dead code found.
evidence.claims: Checked: README/page 'six states' matches calc.mjs STATE_RULES (6 keys) and the HTML title and select. 'Nothing uploaded' is backed by no fetch calls in calc.mjs/index.html (grep) and usage.mjs using localStorage only. Disclaimer present in README, page intro, 'what this does not cover', footer 'No warranty', and as an always-present finding (tested). Not backed or wrong: (a) VENTURE.yaml description and the JSON-LD featureList ('five states') contradict six; (b) FAQ answers (JSON-LD and visible HTML) list only five states, leaving Georgia out; (c) llms.txt links to the retired duncan-haywood.github.io address, not marisstella.app; (d) sitemap.xml and robots.txt use relative URLs ('./index.html', 'Sitemap: ./sitemap.xml'), which search engines do not accept as valid, so the SEO files do not work; (e) README says figures were 'verified' via WebSearch of secondary explainers, and the calc.mjs header admits Georgia's 'statute text not opened', so no figure was checked against statute text, and the 'verified' wording overstates; (f) VENTURE.yaml kill_criteria and hypotheses are untested, which is fine for a prototype and is stated.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job of a California sub who first delivered 2026-03-10, finished 2026-06-20, owner recorded NOC 2026-07-01: tool gives prelim 2026-03-30 and lien 2026-07-31 with a note, which is the right answer, and the 'completion not entered' fallback errs early. A lien specialist would hit gaps in the first hour: no second-tier claimants (a very common user), no CA notice of cessation or direct-contractor clocks (8412 original contractor gets 60 days after NOC), no Texas per-month notice table (only the first month shown, though the TX finding says so), no public-works or bond claims, no holiday handling, and no Texas/Georgia/Florida enforcement-suit deadlines beyond a Georgia note. Within its stated first-tier scope the user can finish the lookup, but not the job of preserving the lien. Prelim date for TX is correct only for the first month of unpaid work, which understates the real need (every month).
evidence.domain: Compared against the structure used by statutory lien practice (Cal. Civ. Code 8200-8204, 8412; Tex. Prop. Code 53.052/53.056; Fla. Stat. 713.06/713.08; A.R.S. 33-992.01/33-993; RCW 60.04.031/091; O.C.G.A. 44-14-361.1/361.5). Good practice shown: first-tier only, cautious direction on unknown completion, weekend rolls back, flags Florida pre-final-payment cutoff and the Georgia 'later of' trigger, and says clearly it is not advice. Departures a specialist would raise: Texas label 'notice of unpaid balance' predates the 2022 reform (statutory term now 'notice of claim for unpaid labor or materials') and the post-2022 Texas lien-clock wording for residential subs was not checked here; a notice-of-completion alone is modelled for CA/AZ but a CA notice of cessation and the 'completion' definition (8180/8182) are not; the Georgia notice is modelled from first furnishing, which is the early safe reading; no state-specific roll-forward rule on weekends (Texas Prop. Code 53.003(e) rolls forward). Sources were secondary explainers, not statute text, which a lawyer would not accept as the basis for a stated deadline.

defects.what: The figures are described as 'verified' but come from secondary lien-service explainers via WebSearch; Georgia's header comment admits statute text was not opened. No deadline was checked against statute text by the author, and this audit could not either (hosts not fetched).

Georgia was added to the calculator but the FAQ (JSON-LD and visible HTML) still lists five states, the JSON-LD featureList and VENTURE.yaml description still say five states: page claims are inconsistent with the tool.
sitemap.xml and robots.txt use relative URLs ('./index.html', 'Sitemap: ./sitemap.xml'); search engines require absolute URLs, so the SEO files do nothing.
llms.txt points to the retired duncan-haywood.github.io address rather than https://marisstella.app/mechanics-lien-deadline-calculator/.

Only first-tier claimants are modelled, and Texas shows only the first month's notice date. Second-tier claimants, who are a large share of real users, get a wrong (too-late) answer with only a general disclaimer.

defects.what: Texas prelimLabel 'notice of unpaid balance' is pre-2022 terminology and should be checked against the current statute.
Tests are example-based only: no property test that safeDate is never later than the statutory date, no cross-check against an external source; Texas residential lien has a single example.

verdict: A small, clean, honest first-tier date calculator whose arithmetic matched my independent recomputation in 8 of 8 cases and whose tests caught all three seeded mutations (including an unsafe-direction sort reversal). It is finished against its own README (six states, weekend and days-left behaviour all work) and its disclaimer is thorough and repeated. It does not meet the bar: correctness is capped at 2 because no figure was checked against statute text (only secondary explainers, and this audit could not reach statute hosts either), claims is 2 because the page, FAQ, JSON-LD, VENTURE.yaml, llms.txt and sitemap/robots files are inconsistent or broken after Georgia was added, and a lien specialist would not sign off on a tool that omits second-tier claimants and Texas per-month notice dates beyond a disclaimer. Fix forward: update the stale five-state text and the FAQ, make sitemap/robots/llms URLs absolute and current, and verify each state against statute text.
